title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: GAR erotema 6 Christ-righteousness parallel tip
pass_a_gloss: Sixth erotema opens: if Adam's sin is ours by imputation as Christ's righteousness is, why is Adam not called our sin as Christ is called our righteousness? GAR: take Scripture's phrases as God gave them; they mark imputation without that title. Placeus: he does not recall owning the question, but it fits to break the major that leans on a strict Christ/Adam same-mode parallel for constituting sinners and righteous. Natural tip into Q6 replies.
pass_b_english: GAR. Sixth it is asked. If as Christ's righteousness is imputed to us, so also Adam's sin is ours by imputation, why is Adam not called our sin as Christ is called our righteousness? Reply 1. That God speaks as He wills; that it is ours to be content with those phrases which occur in the Scriptures, and which set forth God's mind, so far as our salvation is concerned, clearly enough. Although therefore Scripture does not say Adam is our sin, yet it uses those locutions which manifestly mark imputation, of which enough was said before. PLAC. I do not remember using this reason or interrogation, nor do I know whose it is: yet whether mine or another's, it seems fitted to refute the major of the argument on which immediate imputation usually most leans—As we are constituted righteous through Christ, in the same way we were constituted sinners through Adam: for it shows a memorable difference between Christ and Adam.
source_text: GAR. Quaeritur sexto. Si ut Christi justitia nobis imputatur, ita & peccatum Adae nostrum sit imputatione, cur non, ut Christus dicitur justitia nostra, ita & Adamus dicitur peccatum nostrum? Resp. 1. Deum loqui ut vult; nostrum esse iis phrasibus esse contentos, quae in Scripturis occurrunt, quaeque Dei mentem, quantum salutis nostrae interest, satis evidenter exponunt. Quanquam ergo non dicit Scriptura Adamum esse peccatum nostrum; eas tamen locutiones adhibet, quae imputationem manifeste designant, de quo fuse dictum est antea. PLAC. Hac ratione seu interrogatione usum esse me non memini, nec cuius sit novi: sive tamen mea, aut alterius sit, accommodata fuisse videtur ad refellendam majorem argumenti, quo solet imputatio immediata maxime niti, Quemadmodum constituimur justi per Christum, eodem modo constituti sumus peccatores per Adamum: ostendit enim inter Christum & Adamum memorabile discrimen.

choices.choice: Why not 'Adam our sin' as 'Christ our righteousness'; Placeus: breaks same-mode major
